correctness.rationale: Total domination in KG(n,2) is equivalent to absence of 2-vertex covers in the selected edge-family graph. Vertices of degree >=3 are forced into every 2-cover and hence 0/1/2 hubs give disjoint exhaustive obstruction classes C_n,H_n,Q_n. Directly checked the 0-hub component types, 1-hub residual 0/1/2 edges, and 2-hub multinomial categories. For k>=n+1 any 2-covered graph has two degree>=3 hubs giving a unique 2-cover and binomial high-cardinality failure count. Independent enumeration of all 2^10 Petersen and 2^15 KG(6,2) edge subsets matched coefficients and endpoint formulas. All n>=5 follows analytic hub classification.
residual_risks: The all-order proof relies on correct exhaustive hub classification, not a finite bound; Kneser KG(n,2) only.
